title: Run the Actions Runtime product, runtime-adapter, and control-room factory
body:
## Outcome

Operate the existing Actions Runtime factory until the required product/runtime graph is implemented and verified: clean-break MCP Runtime, Community cleanup, RCC-backed local execution, genuinely pluggable Runtime Adapters, immutable Package/Deployment/Run identity, first-class Robots, the lightweight Control Room, and independent workers.

This is the **current execution ledger**. Child issues retain their architecture and full acceptance contracts. Sequencing a node later does not waive its requirements or claim it complete.

## Current execution ledger — 2026-09-07

Architecture roadmap: #82. This issue owns operational sequencing and receipts, not a second architecture plan.
Verified community: `d747d1839b53712937cb9293a34049c89ca507fa`. No open PRs at reconciliation.

### Merged work and remaining acceptance

| Work | Merged implementation | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Configured API-key protection | #199 → #152 | Merged. Retain owning-issue acceptance; no blanket closure. |
| Bounded Robot staging/downloads | #200 → #151 / immediate #148 | Merged; regression/package/Linux native evidence recorded. DNS-rebinding/real SSRF proof remains NOT RUN/UNPROVEN. Later compiler work remains under #148. |
| Explicit Origin/CORS/WebSocket policy | #201 → #153 | Merged; new observed WebSocket disconnect is tracked by #209. |
| Shared SQLite/PostgreSQL abstraction | #109 → #84 | Merged. Full database and packaged acceptance remains distinct from merge. |
| Frontend build, shell and product-evidence harness | #115/#112/#119 → #98/#96/#97 | Merged. Current UX and real packaged-backend quality remain open; #208 is a confirmed released defect. |
| RCC artifact execution/generation work | #197 → #134 | Merged. Full provider/lifecycle/conformance matrix remains open; opt-in artifact execution is not universal adapter completion. |
| Community product cleanup | #128 → #125 | Merged implementation; reconcile retained acceptance rather than repeat cleanup. |
| Release identity, unsigned recovery and publication lookup | #202/#203/#204 | Merged. Native 1.0.1 published; delivery caller migration remains #211. |
| Joshua Yorko metadata and template pins | #205/#206/#207 | Merged and PyPI patches published; all four bundled templates pin Core 1.0.1. |

The September 5 draft/HOLD table is historical and superseded by this ledger. Historical comments and counterexamples remain evidence for their original commits, not instructions to reopen merged PRs. Owning issue checklists stay open until their full acceptance is proven.

### Published surfaces

- **Standalone GitHub Runtime 1.0.1:** immutable tag `actions-runtime-1.0.1` → `0accc8f8cd1590957dec63d94e091aa945653614`; Linux x86_64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64 binaries are published and explicitly unsigned. Public hashes verified; downloaded Linux version/startup/MCP/Action passed. Post-download macOS/Windows execution remains NOT RUN here.
- **PyPI:** Runtime 1.0.2, Core 1.0.1, HTTP helper 1.0.1, Work Items 0.4.4. Fresh combined install/version/metadata/dependency checks and bundled-template pins verified. Runtime PyPI run [34153903999](https://github.com/joshyorko/actions/actions/runs/34153903999) passed.
- Core's original patch workflow [34153664079](https://github.com/joshyorko/actions/actions/runs/34153664079) failed a hardcoded 1.0.0 verifier. #207 fixed the verifier; Core 1.0.1 was published using Poetry after clean-wheel execution and strict artifact validation. The old run stays failed.
- HTTP helper's tag workflow [34153664540](https://github.com/joshyorko/actions/actions/runs/34153664540) received an empty credential; verified Poetry publication completed separately. Future CI delivery is #210, not marked fixed by that upload.
- **Homebrew:** joshyorko/homebrew-tools#103 is CLOSED, completed by Joshua Yorko. The cask now uses Runtime 1.0.1 assets/hashes. Do not reopen it. Actions-side legacy dispatch/CDN/S3 configuration remains #211.
- Native recovery run [34150010615](https://github.com/joshyorko/actions/actions/runs/34150010615) built all three platforms but failed publication cwd/draft lookup; retained binaries were published separately. #204 fixes future lookup/targeting. Do not report that old run green.
- Runtime 1.0.2 was a **PyPI metadata/template update**, not a new standalone GitHub release. Old tags and files remain immutable.
- Actions RCC baseline remains v18.19.3 with intentional v18.18.1 N-1 coverage. RCC release/factory ownership is separate; re-read its released contract before any future repin.

### Immediate execution graph

1. **#208** — repair standalone Work Items loading and truthful UI states; deliver alongside **#96/#97**, under frontend umbrella **#93**.
2. **#209** — diagnose/fix the observed assembled WebSocket Origin test disconnect; related policy owner **#153**. Root cause remains unresolved.
3. **#210** — repair HTTP-helper publishing credential delivery without exposing tokens or republishing existing files.
4. **#211** — finish Actions-owned distribution caller alignment with the completed community Homebrew tap; explicitly settle legacy CDN/S3 targets.
5. **#96/#97/#93** — working product UX, visual polish, accessibility/responsiveness and real packaged-backend errors. These must not wait for **#132/#145**.
6. **#99 + #100 → #127**, with **#71** as Canvas product direction: renderer and Python authoring contract before a working Canvas template. Current shipped Canvas view is a placeholder, not a finished renderer. No separate Canvas PyPI package is established.
7. **#126** — MCP v2 showcase template. The existing stateless MCP implementation is shipped; the showcase remains unimplemented. Reconcile actual #125 cleanup acceptance instead of blindly retaining an obsolete blanket cleanup blocker.

Native GitHub sub-issues register the immediate bugs under #101 and the UX/Canvas/template work under #93. Cross-cutting relations remain explicit links, not artificial blocking dependencies. ACMM/scanner/Hive advisory issues are not the execution queue; do not restore Hive execution labels.

## Architecture invariants

```text
Capability kind          Runtime Adapter          Placement
Action                   RCC                      local process
Robot Task        +      uv                +      container
Workflow                 Python                   independent worker / VM
Dev Task                 Robot Framework          desktop / session
```

RCC is the first/default proving adapter, not the permanent generic schema. Every admitted Run pins a Runtime Plan/adapter before execution; retry, reload, missing cache, and provider failures must not silently change it. A genuinely different adapter must pass #143/#139 before neutrality is claimed.

Package source, adapter runtime artifacts, and Run outputs are distinct. RCC owns its cryptographic Environment Artifact, provider, materialization, leases, and execution contracts; Actions owns capability/deployment/run admission, Attempt fencing, source/binding policy, scheduling, MCP and UI. Namespaced RCC metadata is not mandatory for non-RCC plans. Provider URLs, local paths, PIDs, interpreter/venv/Holotree paths, and container IDs are not portable identities. Package code cannot install adapters or grant itself sockets, mounts, roots, credentials, or exposure policy.

## Bounded execution policy

Use the existing controller and worker topology, not a new orchestrator. Keep **at most two implementation writers active**, each with an isolated worktree and disjoint production-file ownership. Reuse existing owners. Read-only verification may proceed independently. Serialize shared `_server.py`, package/lock files, `tasks.py`, and canonical guidance integration. Do not broaden merge/release/credential authority.

Queue only dependency-ready bounded tasks. Fix one reproduced boundary at a time with RED/GREEN evidence. A blocked lane does not freeze an unrelated lane, but a green test subset does not authorize removing a required gate.

## Retained acceptance after merged foundations

The owning issues preserve their full contracts. Implementation is merged; unfinished acceptance is not erased:

- **#152/#153:** assembled protected/public router, streaming, browser and actual authentication-mode coverage. #209 owns the newly observed disconnect; CORS is not authentication.
- **#151/#148:** retain original outside-root regression and bounded streaming/extraction/atomic publication proof. Complete real URL/DNS-rebinding assurance; the later immutable compiler/second-adapter checkpoint is separate.
- **#84:** complete SQLite/PostgreSQL driver semantics, fresh/concurrent/legacy migrations, collision/data preservation, rollback/rerun, too-new rejection, conditional writes/database time, secret-safe failure handling and source/wheel/frozen proof. Old pre-merge lexer findings require current-code verification, not automatic reopening.
- **#134/#133:** complete real provider A-to-B/provider-dead warm reuse, pinned identity on reacquisition, corrupt/incompatible rejection, lease/drain/cancellation/reaping, restart migration, source/wheel/frozen and explicit skip classification. Preserve generation pinning and atomic scheduler/MCP catalog publication. Historical environment failures are not presumed present on today's commit.
- **#98/#96/#97:** preserve validated dual artifacts, inventories/SBOMs/offline behavior, functioning routes, accurate state/error UX and authentic browser/accessibility/visual evidence. Fixture product evidence is not live-backend acceptance; #208 demonstrates why that distinction matters.
- **#125/#154:** preserve legal attribution/history and verify remaining active product/package/documentation cleanup. Published author/README corrections do not prove every runtime docstring or historical link was cleaned.

No merged foundation PR must remain draft or be re-created. Continue only from a current reproduced defect or a still-unproved acceptance row.

## Wave D onward — consume proven contracts, do not abandon the roadmap

These remain required later graph outcomes, not blanket deferrals:

1. **#143 + #139:** derive the generic plan/preflight seam from working #134, then prove a genuinely different uv/direct Robot Framework adapter with the same no-fallback conformance. Avoid a speculative plugin framework.
2. **#130 + #135:** stabilize immutable adapter-neutral Package/capability/runtime-plan identity and the compiler. **#148's second checkpoint** then converges shipping imports and finite legacy `~/.robots` migration through that compiler. **#136** adds source registry/cache publication. Package/source identity must not force RCC Environment Artifacts onto non-RCC adapters.
3. **#129 + #83:** after #84 and the required immutable plan/deployment contracts, implement Deployment revisions and Run/Attempt authority/fencing/reconciliation. Do not resurrect old PR #107. **#85** exposes MCP Tasks backed by those Runs, not a second queue.
4. **#144/#145/#146:** first-class Robot Tasks with optional Work Items, the truthful lightweight Control Room/Run Composer, and common-service CLI. Preserve working local product behavior during migration; do not fork a second Robot administration application.
5. **#196:** collapsed RCC provider convenience comes after #134, the supported `joshyorko/rcc#208` server surface, and #152/#153 exposure safety. Supervise/proxy RCC's real loopback child with bounded streaming, auth, disconnect/range semantics, and real A-to-B proof. It is optional for ordinary local execution and never owns Runs or a shared writable Holotree. Gate any verify/repair/GC controls on the actual safe RCC contract. #145 may consume this focused component without making the whole Control Room a prerequisite.
6. **#147/#142:** internal parent-child capability invocation and execution matrices follow stable admission/lifetime contracts; prove no nested-capacity deadlock, silent adapter switching, host-socket escape, or simulated support.
7. **#90/#138:** independent ordinary workers and a versioned worker protocol after durable admission/fencing. First distributed proof is Runtime replicas + PostgreSQL + ordinary workers with local caches; no mandatory broker/Kubernetes.
8. **#86/#87/#131/#132/#140/#141:** output/binding/secret/data/Work Item providers, operations, and workflows consume the same admitted identities and lifetime authority. Do not rebuild proprietary Data Server, use Work Items as all Run ownership, or turn semantic roles into mandatory services.
9. **#71/#99/#100:** Canvas/MCP App View and author-facing surfaces consume canonical Package/Deployment/Run contracts and the validated #98 artifacts. Optional skill/distribution surfaces are not core execution dependencies. **#91/#92** retain their explicit MCP auth/interaction contracts separately from immediate API-key correctness.

## Remaining issue disposition

- **#125:** reconcile actual cleanup/template/packaging acceptance against current code; retain until its required rows are proven. #126/#127 consume the accepted template/example/Canvas boundaries, not an obsolete cleanup PR.
- **#149:** keep the living advisory issue; advisory findings are not automatic implementation/merge authority.
- **#150:** closed as invalid unfilled CI template, **not fixed**; actual CI failures belong with #98/#115 and their exact run evidence.
- **#154/#155:** reconcile package examples/canonical roadmap with current behavior and this ledger; no second execution backlog.
- **#162:** evaluate real equivalent coverage/gates; no dummy filenames or threshold gaming to satisfy a scanner.
- **#194/#195:** cover the identified command/scope paths and review cross-package API dependencies with source/wheel/frozen evidence when touching those seams; no opportunistic full-repository rewrite.

## Evidence, integration, and completion

Maintain one compact requirement ledger: issue/criterion -> owner/PR -> exact source SHA -> test/runtime command -> platform/binary/fixture identity -> result -> remaining dependency. PASS, BLOCKED, and NOT RUN must remain distinct. Record source changed, built, runtime verified, pushed, merged, and released separately.

Use current repository-local skills/toolkit, native acceptance where required, disjoint worktrees, bounded subprocesses, RED/GREEN counterexamples, current-base integration tests, and independent exact-head review. Generated assets come from canonical tasks; do not fix setup failures with hidden mocks or skips. Preserve existing controller/human merge and release boundaries. No tag/release/branch-protection changes are implied by graph triage.

The next useful checkpoint is the immediate #208–#211 defect/delivery graph and working #96/#97 UX, while retaining the dependency-ordered architecture work below #82. A checkpoint is not program closure. This issue closes only when its required child roadmap is actually accepted, including the second adapter, pinned retry/replica semantics, collapsed/independent-worker topology, and truthful UI/CLI operation. Preserve unresolved rows instead of manufacturing completion receipts.
